answer: The orchard multiplier is published, charged in gale, and kernel lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2800 identities would post 2491 proofs and burn roughly 29 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
